items.title: Allen Toussaint Interview, 1979-03-13
items.q: There was a whole era of things like doing the Shirley Ellis days

ctx.x: New Orleans, I think, in the 60s had a lot of novelty records that sewed really well. I guess they were called novelty then. And Huey Smith told me that he thought that the music and musical games that children play just on the streets really, he thinks that really has a big influence or did have a big influence on New Orleans music then. What do you feel about that?

Well, here I can certainly afford to speak of that because he was such a mess that those novelty type tunes. I can see a correlation there. There was a whole era of things like doing the Shirley Ellis days of Banana Banner for Fenn and things like that. And they had a lot of these and Purple People Eater even. So those that I consider novelty. I guess in the whole general sense, yes, they do have a lot to do with the street. A lot of novelty tunes that I've written that turned out to be novelty. I didn't…

Okay. At that time, it seemed like almost all the New Orleans music that we know today was being written by you like It's Raining and Ruler of My Heart and Over You. Did you write those songs specifically with, okay, did you write It's Raining with Irma Thomas in mind or did she come to you and say, connect me up with something that I'll be able to sing well? How did that go? How did that go?
